items.title: [@highcharts/dashboards] Highcharts Grid: `javascript:` URL in credits.href runs script on click
items.summary: ImpactAn attacker who controls the Grid configuration can set credits.href to a javascript: URL. The value is not validated against an allowed-scheme list before it is applied to the credits link, so activating that link runs attacker-supplied script in the origin of the page hosting the Grid. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Grid configuration and that a user activate the credits link. Script running this way has the same access to page data, storage and session state as the hosting application.WorkaroundsPaste in after the Grid Pro module is imported, before a Grid is created.const { AST } = Grid;function sanitize(options) {    const credits = options && options.credits;    if (credits && typeof credits.href === 'string') {        const filtered = AST.filterUserAttributes({ href: credits.href });        if (!filtered.href) {            delete credits.href;        }    }    return options;}// Both Grid.grid() and grid.update() funnel through loadUserOptions, so one// hook covers both entry points.const { prototype } = Grid.Grid;const loadUserOptions = prototype.loadUserOptions;prototype.loadUserOptions = function (options, ...rest) {    sanitize(options);    return loadUserOptions.call(this, options, ...rest);};Obtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install @highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0. If you load Highcharts Grid from a CDN, use a versioned URL, for example https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0/grid-lite.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-6hgp-fmhr-mrg4https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/pull/25351https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/45b74403acafbe9f621c4a343506721d9129e991https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/grid-v3.2.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6hgp-fmhr-mrg4

items.title: [@highcharts/grid-lite] Highcharts Grid parses pagination language options as HTML
items.summary: ImpactThe pagination language strings are written into the DOM as markup rather than as text. An attacker who controls those language options can supply elements carrying event handlers, and those handlers execute in the origin of the page hosting the Grid when the pagination controls render. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Grid language configuration and that pagination be enabled on the Grid.WorkaroundsRun this once after loading the Grid, before creating any grid:{    const Pagination = Grid.Pagination;    const escapeLang = (pagination) => {        const lang = pagination.lang;        if (!lang) {            return;        }        for (const key of ['pageInfo', 'pageSizeLabel']) {            if (typeof lang[key] === 'string') {                lang[key] = lang[key].replace(/</g, '<');            }        }    };    for (const name of ['updatePageInfo', 'renderPageSizeSelector']) {        const original = Pagination.prototype[name];        Pagination.prototype[name] = function (...args) {            escapeLang(this);            return original.apply(this, args);        };    }}Obtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install @highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0. If you load Highcharts Grid from a CDN, use a versioned URL, for example https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0/grid-lite.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-r5wg-q8fc-p6w2https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/1e8ded84d52191883965641b863cf0c73eb759aahttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/grid-v3.2.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r5wg-q8fc-p6w2

items.title: [@highcharts/dashboards] Highcharts Dashboards parses fullscreen labels as HTML
items.summary: ImpactThe edit mode fullscreen labels are parsed as HTML when the corresponding control is rendered. An attacker who controls the Dashboards language options can supply markup carrying event handlers, which then execute in the origin of the page hosting the dashboard. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Dashboards language configuration and that the affected control be rendered. Script running this way has the same access to page data, storage and session state as the hosting application.WorkaroundsUntil you can upgrade, replace Fullscreen.prototype.setButtonText atapplication startup. The replacement is the original method with textContent in place of innerHTML.If you install Dashboards from npmImport the module once, before any board is created.import Fullscreen from '@highcharts/dashboards/es-modules/Dashboards/EditMode/Fullscreen.js';Fullscreen.prototype.setButtonText = function () {    const editMode = this.board.editMode,        button = editMode?.tools.contextMenu?.items.viewFullscreen;    if (button?.innerElement) {        const lang = editMode.lang;        button.innerElement.textContent =            (this.isOpen ? lang.exitFullscreen : lang.viewFullscreen) || '';    }};If you load Dashboards from a <script> tagThe same replacement, taking Fullscreen from the global namespace. It must run after modules/layout and before any board is created.<script src="https://code.highcharts.com/dashboards/dashboards.js"></script><script src="https://code.highcharts.com/dashboards/modules/layout.js"></script><script>{    const Fullscreen = window.Dashboards?.Fullscreen;    Fullscreen.prototype.setButtonText = function () {        const editMode = this.board.editMode,            button = editMode?.tools.contextMenu?.items.viewFullscreen;        if (button?.innerElement) {            const lang = editMode.lang;            button.innerElement.textContent =                (this.isOpen ? lang.exitFullscreen : lang.viewFullscreen) || '';        }    };}</script>If your application does not need Edit Mode, leaving it disabled (editMode.enabled: false) removes the exposure as well. The same applies to the context menu — the label is only reachable when viewFullscreen is among editMode.contextMenu.items.Obtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install @highcharts/dashboards@4.2.3. If you load Highcharts Dashboards from a CDN, use a versioned URL, for example https://code.highcharts.com/dashboards/4.2.3/dashboards.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-58g7-7f52-h92chttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/f97213bab745e40f628720c21f4e8b31ee3e768bhttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/dashboards-v4.2.3https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-58g7-7f52-h92c

items.title: [@highcharts/dashboards] Highcharts Dashboards parses sidebar component labels as HTML
items.summary: ImpactThe component language strings shown in the edit mode sidebar are parsed as HTML rather than inserted as text. An attacker who controls those language options can supply markup carrying event handlers, which execute in the origin of the page hosting the dashboard once the sidebar renders the affected labels. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Dashboards language configuration and that a user open the edit mode sidebar.WorkaroundsUntil you can upgrade, patch EditMode once at application startup. The hook runs before the sidebar is built, so the labels are already harmless by the time they are rendered. Assigning a string to textContent and reading back innerHTML turns any markup into literal text, which is exactly what the fixed version renders.After importing the module, use this code snipped once, before any board is created.{    const EditMode = window.Dashboards?.EditMode;    const escapeHTML = (text) => text        .replace(/&/g, '&')        .replace(/</g, '<')        .replace(/>/g, '>');    const patched = new WeakSet();    const originalInit = EditMode.prototype.init;    EditMode.prototype.init = function (...args) {        const labels = this.lang?.sidebar;        if (labels && !patched.has(this)) {            patched.add(this);            for (const key of Object.keys(labels)) {                if (typeof labels[key] === 'string') {                    labels[key] = escapeHTML(labels[key]);                }            }        }        return originalInit.apply(this, args);    };}If your application does not need Edit Mode, leaving it disabled (editMode.enabled: false) removes the exposure as well.Obtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install @highcharts/dashboards@4.2.3. If you load Highcharts Dashboards from a CDN, use a versioned URL, for example https://code.highcharts.com/dashboards/4.2.3/dashboards.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-rcqf-f6h2-ccg9https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/e65f8c21b9974dcccfa1c600a375d836acef4a7dhttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/dashboards-v4.2.3https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rcqf-f6h2-ccg9

items.title: [highcharts] Highcharts: dotted series.keys paths write to Object.prototype
items.summary: ImpactA dot-separated key path taken from series.keys is followed without filtering the individual segments. An attacker who controls series.keys and the matching point data can use a path such as __proto__.polluted to set arbitrary properties on Object.prototype. The resulting properties are visible to all JavaScript running in the page, not only to the chart. No user interaction is required beyond rendering the chart.The injected properties are inert until other code on the page reads them, so consequences depend on the consuming application.WorkaroundsDrop-in fix - for any versions affected (6.1.0-13.0.2). Add the below IIFE to run after Highcharts is loaded.((H)=>{const X = H.isObject;H.Point.prototype.setNestedProperty = function setNestedProperty(t,e,i){let s=i.split(".");return s.some(t=>"__proto__"===t||"constructor"===t)||s.reduce(function(t,i,s,o){let r=o.length-1===s;return t[i]=r?e:X(t[i],!0)?t[i]:{},t[i]},t),t};})(Highcharts);Live demo & testingObtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install highcharts@13.1.1. If you load Highcharts from the CDN, use the versioned URLs on code.highcharts.com, for example https://code.highcharts.com/13.1.1/highcharts.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-rmqc-xvr3-v46chttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-118250https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/pull/25313https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/fd4ee8140732618bbe71295aba55398fb1f8fa9ehttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/v13.1.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rmqc-xvr3-v46c

items.title: [highcharts] Highcharts: series column construction writes to Object.prototype
items.summary: ImpactWhen series columns are built from point objects, the point option keys are used directly as data column ids, so the write that populates a column reaches Object.prototype and the Object constructor. Keys named __proto__ and constructor survive JSON.parse as own enumerable properties, so an attacker who controls the point objects can set integer-keyed properties on Object.prototype, one per point index, to values of their choosing. Named properties cannot be reached this way. The integer keys still affect every object in the page: reading an out-of-range index on any array or plain object returns the attacker's value, and for...in over any object yields the injected keys, so unrelated code can take branches it should not using attacker-supplied data, and rendering can fail as a side effect. The properties remain in place once the chart has been built, and no user interaction is required beyond rendering the chart.Consequences beyond disruption depend on the consuming application.WorkaroundsDrop-in fix - for any versions affected (6.1.0-13.0.2).Add the below IIFE to run after Highcharts is loaded.;!function(t){if(t&&t.Point&&!t.Point.prototype.protoPollutionPatched){var o=t.Point.prototype,r=o.optionsToObject,e=o.setNestedProperty,n=Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty;o.optionsToObject=function(t){if(t&&"object"==typeof t&&!Array.isArray(t)&&(n.call(t,"__proto__")||n.call(t,"constructor"))){var o={};for(var e in t)n.call(t,e)&&!c(e)&&(o[e]=t[e]);t=o}return r.call(this,t)},o.setNestedProperty=function(t,o,r){return String(r).split(".").some(c)?t:e.call(this,t,o,r)},o.protoPollutionPatched=!0}function c(t){return"__proto__"===t||"constructor"===t}}(Highcharts);Live demo & testingObtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install highcharts@13.1.0. If you load Highcharts from the CDN, use the versioned URLs on code.highcharts.com, for example https://code.highcharts.com/13.1.0/highcharts.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-gfvx-2c2g-38wqhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-118249https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/pull/25321https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/d3357705c8f348904441327e32f50ab528c3a205https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/v13.1.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gfvx-2c2g-38wq

items.title: [highcharts] Highcharts Core: `breadcrumbs.style` keys become SVG event-handler attributes
items.summary: ImpactThe breadcrumbs style option is applied to the breadcrumb button as SVG attributes rather than as CSS, and the attribute names are not filtered. An attacker who controls the chart configuration can supply keys under breadcrumbs.style that name event handlers, and those keys become live handlers on the breadcrumb button, so the attacker's script runs in the origin of the page hosting the chart. The option is reached through drilldown.breadcrumbs, navigation.breadcrumbs and the breadcrumbs option of the treemap, sunburst and treegraph series. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the chart configuration and that a user drill down, or traverse into a level of a hierarchical series, so that the breadcrumbs render, and then hover over or activate the breadcrumb button. Charts rendered in styled mode do not apply the option and are not affected. Charts built with Highcharts Stock, Maps and Gantt are included, since those ship from the same package as Core.WorkaroundsVerified against published bundles on 10.0.0, 11.4.8, 12.3.0 and 13.0.2.Load immediately after Highcharts, before any chart is created:// Workaround fix for all affected Highcharts versions: 10.0.0-13.0.2((H)=>{const S=H.SVGElement.prototype,D=S._defaultSetter;S._defaultSetter=function _defaultSetter(v,k,e){/^on/i.test(k)||D.call(this,v,k,e)};})(Highcharts);// End of the workaround fixObtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install highcharts@13.1.0. If you load Highcharts from the CDN, use the versioned URLs on code.highcharts.com, for example https://code.highcharts.com/13.1.0/highcharts.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-35rr-xwfh-x789https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-118246https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/b0fafdaaee7d0cac2ecfeb0eaf37b11cd40594efhttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/releases/tag/v13.1.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-35rr-xwfh-x789

items.title: [@highcharts/grid-pro] Highcharts Grid Pro: cell-renderer `attributes` map written with raw `setAttribute`
items.summary: ImpactThe input-type cell renderers copy every entry of the renderer's attributes option onto the input or select element they create, without checking the attribute names. An attacker who controls the Grid configuration can supply entries under a column's cells.renderer.attributes or cells.editMode.renderer.attributes whose names are event handlers, and those handlers execute in the origin of the page hosting the Grid. A view renderer places the handler on the input rendered in every row of the column as soon as the Grid renders; an edit-mode renderer places it on the input created when a cell enters edit mode, and that input is focused immediately, so a focus handler runs as soon as the user starts editing. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Grid configuration and that a user hover over or focus one of the rendered inputs, or begin editing a cell. The Pro DataGrid that shipped inside the Dashboards package is included.WorkaroundsIf your column configuration comes from a source you do not fully control, paste this snippet right after importing the Grid module:const ALLOWED_RENDERER_ATTRIBUTES = [    'autofocus', 'checked', 'max', 'maxlength', 'min', 'minlength',    'multiple', 'pattern', 'placeholder', 'size', 'step'];const scrubColumn = (column) => {    const cells = column?.cells;    for (const renderer of [cells?.renderer, cells?.editMode?.renderer]) {        const attributes = renderer?.attributes;        if (attributes) {            for (const key of Object.keys(attributes)) {                if (!ALLOWED_RENDERER_ATTRIBUTES.includes(key.toLowerCase())) {                    delete attributes[key];                }            }        }    }    return column;};const scrubOptions = (options) => {    scrubColumn(options?.columnDefaults);    (options?.columns || []).forEach(scrubColumn);    return options;};const proto = Grid.Grid.prototype;const loadUserOptions = proto.loadUserOptions;proto.loadUserOptions = function (options, ...rest) {    scrubOptions(Grid.defaultOptions);    return loadUserOptions.call(this, scrubOptions(options), ...rest);};const updateColumn = proto.updateColumn;proto.updateColumn = function (columnId, options, ...rest) {    return updateColumn.call(this, columnId, scrubColumn(options), ...rest);};Obtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install @highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0. If you load Highcharts Grid from a CDN, use a versioned URL, for example https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0/grid-lite.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-5ghw-9mgr-jvx2https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-116797https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/52abd4f8f8db87dd20eab7c01444112380e30e98https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5ghw-9mgr-jvx2

items.title: [@highcharts/grid-lite] Highcharts Grid: custom icon definition objects written with raw `setAttribute` on `<path>`
items.summary: ImpactA custom icon supplied under rendering.icons as an icon definition object is built by creating an SVG path for each of its child entries and setting every key of that entry as an attribute of the path, without filtering the attribute names; only the string form of the option is passed through the markup allow-list. An attacker who controls the Grid configuration can therefore supply child entries whose keys name event handlers, and those handlers execute in the origin of the page hosting the Grid. Custom icons take precedence over the built-in ones, so the attacker can replace icons that render without any further configuration, such as the sort icon shown in every column header by default and the pagination controls where pagination is enabled, and does not need any reference to a custom icon name. Exploitation requires that untrusted data reach the Grid configuration and that a user hover over or activate an affected icon.WorkaroundsIf your Grid configuration comes from a source you do not fully control, paste this snippet right after importing the Grid module:(function () {    const GridNS = typeof Grid !== 'undefined' ? Grid : undefined;    const GridClass = GridNS && GridNS.Grid;    if (!GridClass || !GridClass.prototype.loadUserOptions) {        return; // Grid not loaded    }    const allowedPathAttributes = [        'd',        'fill',        'opacity',        'stroke',        'stroke-width',        'stroke-linecap',        'stroke-linejoin',        'transform'    ];    const originalLoadUserOptions = GridClass.prototype.loadUserOptions;    function sanitizeIconValue(value) {        if (!value || typeof value === 'string') {            return value;        }        const children = value.children || [];        const sanitizedChildren = [];        for (let i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {            const child = children[i] || {};            const clean = {};            for (let j = 0; j < allowedPathAttributes.length; j++) {                const attr = allowedPathAttributes[j];                if (child[attr] !== undefined && child[attr] !== null) {                    clean[attr] = child[attr];                }            }            sanitizedChildren.push(clean);        }        return {            width: value.width,            height: value.height,            viewBox: value.viewBox,            fill: value.fill,            children: sanitizedChildren        };    }    function sanitizeIconsMap(icons) {        if (!icons) {            return icons;        }        const out = {};        for (const key in icons) {            if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(icons, key)) {                out[key] = sanitizeIconValue(icons[key]);            }        }        return out;    }    GridClass.prototype.loadUserOptions = function (newOptions) {        if (            newOptions &&            newOptions.rendering &&            newOptions.rendering.icons        ) {            newOptions.rendering.icons = sanitizeIconsMap(                newOptions.rendering.icons            );        }        return originalLoadUserOptions.apply(this, arguments);    };}());Obtaining the patched versionThe patched releases are available from all the usual distribution channels. With npm, upgrade the affected package to the patched version listed above, for example npm install @highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0. If you load Highcharts Grid from a CDN, use a versioned URL, for example https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@highcharts/grid-lite@3.2.0/grid-lite.js. For more on each installation method, see the installation guide.Referenceshttps://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/security/advisories/GHSA-6g3c-p4fg-xv47https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-118242https://github.com/highcharts/highcharts/commit/8fc970658fee6601625b42da29d27c3ef7c45e30https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6g3c-p4fg-xv47
